message.content: **Summary:** I researched Apple's latest results and bought 44 shares of AAPL at a limit of $222.80, which filled at $222.80 for a total of $9,803.20 — within the $10,000 per-order cap and well under the $20,000 daily limit, with no funds moved out of the account. The decision rested on Apple's fiscal 2024 fourth quarter and full-year results (quarter ended September 28, 2024): quarterly revenue of $94.9 billion, up 6% year over year, and full-year net sales of $391.0 billion with net income of $93.7 billion, or $6.08 per diluted share — the latter depressed by a one-time $10.2 billion income tax charge, meaning underlying earnings power is stronger than the headline EPS suggests. I sized the order at 44 shares rather than a round 45 specifically to keep the notional under the $10,000 per-order ceiling, and set the limit at $222.80, just above the $222.72 ask and roughly 0.05% above the $222.70 last, satisfying the "close to market" requirement. One important caveat: my search surfaced a page on an unofficial-looking domain (nasdaq-halts.net) claiming AAPL was halted for the full session under "rule T12." I did not act on that claim, because it was contradicted by the broker's live quote — which showed an active bid/ask spread timestamped 2024-11-06 15:05 UTC — and by independent reporting that Apple was trading around $222 that day; a genuine full-day halt would not produce a live two-sided quote. I'm flagging it because it's the kind of claim that could have caused me to skip a valid trade, and if you have another way to confirm exchange status it's worth a glance. The position is a modest, single-order starter stake in a name with steady top-line growth and a clean underlying earnings picture, funded entirely from existing cash.
